Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Payment schedule proposal for Redwood services

Hi Markus / Laura,

Thanks for the productive workshop last week — Luma is excited to move forward with Redwood for inference in our protein design pipeline. Procurement is ready to issue a PO but we need to lock down payment terms and a credit ceiling before we route for approvals.

High-level ask from finance:
- Preferred: Net60 with a 60-day payment stability window (aligns to existing vendor terms)
- If Redwood requires shorter terms initially, we can do a staged approach (e.g., Net45 after the first quarter)
- Credit limit target: $250,000 (to cover expected burst months)

Attached our preliminary PO (Luma_PO_12587.pdf) — it references Net60. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept Net60 with a 90-day ramp fallback and how you handle VAT for our EU subsidiary (we will route invoicing to the US entity but may request VAT evidence later).

Next steps we need from Redwood procurement: a short written summary of the staged-payment proposal and any required deposit/retainer.

Thanks,
Sophie Patel
Procurement Lead, Luma Therapeutics

Subject: Re: Payment schedule proposal for Redwood services

Sophie — thanks for the PO and the clear asks. We’re very enthusiastic to get Luma live. Below is a pragmatic proposal that balances Luma’s cash cadence and Redwood’s growth-stage credit controls.

Proposal (staged remit + conditional credit corridor):
1) Initial tranche: 20% retainer invoiced on kickoff (due Net30) — secures capacity and covers initial provisioning.
2) Ongoing usage: monthly invoicing thereafter on Net45 for months 1–3.
3) After month 3, if usage and payments are on track (no delinquencies), move to Net60 and increase credit ceiling to $250k.
4) If collection risk appears (late payments >15 days on 2 consecutive invoices), automatic rollback to Net30 and hold of burst capacity until arrears cleared.

Commercials/discounts: 1.5% early-pay discount if an invoice is paid within 10 days.

VAT / tax handling:
- We can invoice Luma US (Redwood US EIN) by default. For EU VAT evidence or reverse-charge requests, we’ll need your EU VAT number and a billing contact — we’ll route to Finance to produce the appropriate VAT-exempt invoice variant.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short one-page summary for your procurement team: Redwood_Luma_Staggered_Terms_v1.pdf

Action items:
- Sophie: confirm you can accept the 20% kickoff retainer and the Net45 initial window.
- Laura/Naomi: please run a soft credit check and provide an estimated time to enable the $250k corridor if approved.
- Ben: please add the early-pay discount clause to the SOW redline.

Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

—Markus Klein
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
Attachment: Redwood_Luma_Staggered_Terms_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 12KB)
From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@luma-thera.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Sophie Patel <sophie@luma-thera.com>, procurement@luma-thera.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment schedule proposal for Redwood services

Markus / Laura — thanks for the quick reply and the helpful structure. A few counterpoints from Luma finance:

Counter-proposal from Luma:
- Kickoff retainer: 20% is acceptable, but we need that invoice Net45 rather than Net30 to align with our internal cashflow.
- Ongoing: move to Net45 for months 1–6 (we can revisit at month 6 for Net60).
- Credit limit: we can approve $150,000 initially and will consider a staged uplift to $250,000 after 3 billing cycles with on-time payments.
- Early-pay: we can take advantage of the 1.5% discount if it’s applied to Net45 / Net30 accelerated payment windows.

VAT note: Luma has a small EU subsidiary (Luma EU BV). For any EU invoices we’ll request reverse-charge/invoice without VAT — I’ll send EU VAT number and the contact for Finance to liaise. For now route invoices to Luma US.

We’ve attached an updated PO with the 20% retainer called out and the Net45 language. Please confirm acceptance and I’ll start internal approvals.

Thanks,
Carlos Ruiz
Senior Finance Manager, Luma Therapeutics
c.ruiz@luma-thera.com
